findings.title: Discover upsampling is enabled for mixed and negated event-type queries
findings.body: The Discover eligibility check is a substring match for `event.type:error`, rather than establishing that the query can only return errors. Queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` contain that substring but can return transactions (which do not have the error sampling weight). Those requests will be rewritten to `upsampled_count()`, producing a weighted/missing-value total instead of the requested event count. Parse or otherwise constrain the event-type condition so the rewrite only occurs when every returned event is known to be an error.

findings.title: Eligibility is checked against the outer dataset rather than the dataset being queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` accepts `scoped_dataset`, including calls made for dashboard split queries, but passes the captured outer `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the metrics-enhanced dashboard split path, an error-only query is executed against `discover` while the captured dataset remains a metrics dataset, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns false and the error result is not upsampled. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the eligibility check so the decision describes the query that will actually execute.

findings.title: Weighted counts are truncated to integers
findings.body: `upsampled_count` wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`. Sampling rates are represented as floats (the added test factory explicitly converts `client_sample_rate` to `float`), and rates such as 0.3 produce non-integral inverse weights. Casting the aggregate truncates the estimate, systematically undercounting every bucket; summing multiple fractional weights can also lose a full event. Return the sum as a numeric value, or use an explicitly specified rounding policy if integer output is required.

findings.title: The PR accidentally adds a gitlink pinned to the base commit
findings.body: This entry is a submodule/gitlink pointing at the base revision, but no corresponding `.gitmodules` configuration is included. Clones of this revision will receive an uninitialized `sentry-repo` directory and tooling may attempt to initialize an undefined submodule. Remove this unrelated repository entry unless adding a properly configured submodule is intentional.
